transcript.speaker: Thomas Kudsk
transcript.title: IR Team
transcript.content: This is Thomas Kudsk Larsen with the IR team. Welcome to the Q2 2024 Conference Call for investors and analysts. As usual, you can find the slides on sanofi.com. Please turn to slide 3. Here we have the usual forward-looking statements. We'd like to remind you that the information presented in this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to substantial risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially. We encourage you to read the disclaimer in our slide presentation. Additionally, we refer you to the Form 20-F filed with the US SEC on the d’Enregistrement document for a description of these risk factors. As usual, we’ll be making comments on our performance using constant statements and other non-IFRS measures. Numbers used are in million euros and for Q2 2024 unless stated otherwise. Please turn to slide 4. First, we have a presentation and then we will take your questions. We have kept the presentation short as other companies report today and we aim to keep the call to a maximum of one hour. For Q&A, we have Brian, Olivier, Thomas, and Julie to cover the global business units and Roy, our General Counsel. For the Q&A, you have two options in Zoom: raise your hand or submit your questions using the Q&A function. With that, I’ll hand over to Paul.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Well, thank you, Thomas. It's so much better when you do the intro. Thank you and hello to everyone on the call. Our strong business momentum continued in the second quarter. We delivered double-digit sales growth at CER and we continue to execute on our former launches while advancing our pipeline of new medicines. Our growth was driven by a strong quarter for Dupixent, seven years into its launch and the broad-based performance of our new medicines. Our vaccine sales were stable when excluding the effect of last year's COVID sales. The sales of Opella, the new name for our consumer healthcare business, grew by 10% with the U.S. Wellness brand Qunol as the main driver in the United States. Based on the robust growth we've seen in the first half, we are confident about the strong business outlook for the remainder of the year, and that's why we are upgrading our earnings per share guidance for 2024, and François will provide more details shortly. Turning to slide 6, Dupixent reached a significant new milestone, with sales exceeding the EUR 3 billion mark in a single quarter for the first time. This new quarterly sales record highlights continued strong volume growth across approved indications, age groups, and geographies. Dupixent’s growth of 29% in the quarter was fueled by its consistent and robust U.S. performance. The rapid expansion in key markets outside the U.S., such as Japan, China, and Europe, further boosted Q2 performance, growing at almost double the pace as the U.S. Looking ahead, we remain excited by the near-to-mid-term growth outlook for Dupixent, bolstered by upcoming regulatory catalysts inside and outside the U.S. We've recently obtained EU approval for COPD. I'm looking forward to the U.S. PDUFA decision at the end of September, which is expected to be a significant driver for Dupixent’s continued expansion. Overall, we are on track for our target of around EUR 13 billion in 2024, in line with our low double-digit compound annual growth rate goal set from 2023 to 2030. Now on slide 7, turning to our launches and how we bring innovation to patients, quarter after quarter, the growth of these new medicines increasingly contributes to our top-line growth. François will explain the key contributions of these successful launches to the accelerated business dynamics shortly. Growth of Nexviazyme due to patients converting from legacy treatments in the Pompe franchise remains a key driver. Most eligible patients in the U.S. are now on the new standard of care with Nexviazyme, and patients continue to convert outside the U.S. ALTUVIIIO has had a strong launch since the end of March. Growth rates remain very strong, with high sales predominantly in the U.S. where it was driven by patient switches. Other medicines also did well in absolute terms, including Sarclisa’s fast expansion in Europe and Japan. As expected, Beyfortus sales in Q2 were low due to vaccine seasonality. Looking ahead to the upcoming RSV season in the Northern Hemisphere, we remain excited by the opportunity for Beyfortus to advance towards all-inform protection and reach blockbuster status globally in 2024. As a world leader in flu vaccines, Sanofi has a pivotal role to play in bringing forward innovative solutions against this disease by addressing current challenges and building strategic partnerships. We have recently announced a new partnership to combine Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine with our differentiated flu vaccines, aiming to create a best-in-class combination. This new combination will include our flu vaccines that have proven efficacy in preventing flu infections and its severe consequences, such as pneumonia and hospitalizations, and has received an ACIP referential recommendation. We believe our truly differentiated combo vaccine will demonstrate favorable tolerability compared to current COVID-19 mRNA-based combination vaccine candidates, ultimately driving higher vaccine rates. To clarify, we believe that combination vaccines developed by competitors that would compromise tolerability or proven levels of efficacy would damage vaccine confidence and negatively impact vaccination rates. Additionally, Sanofi will commercialize Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine from next year and book the sales. Thanks to our leading commercial capabilities, we hope to be able to further drive broader acceptance of COVID-19 immunization. Considering the recent public concern about H5N1 avian influenza, we take responsibility in pandemic preparedness with two pivotal programs. Our egg-based protein adjuvanted vaccine is set to begin a study in Q3 in collaboration with BARDA, and our mRNA pandemic flu program will enter clinical studies in the coming months. In summary, our commitment to innovation continues to drive our leadership in the flu vaccine market, ensuring we are prepared to meet current and future challenges. Well, let me conclude by highlighting a separate positive note relating to our ESG commitment. Time magazine recently ranked Sanofi as the world's seventh most sustainable company across industries and first in pharma. This ranking reflects the progress of our integrated ESG strategy, and thanks to our comprehensive carbon transition plan, we are now on track to meet carbon neutrality in 2023 in line with our science-based target initiative commitment. To achieve this target, we are focusing on key decarbonization levels presented on the slide. For Scopes 1 and 2, a 43% reduction of our activities was already achieved, and we are targeting a 55% reduction by 2030. For Scope 3, a 10% reduction has been accomplished so far, and we're aiming for a 30% reduction across our value chain. With that, I hand over to François.

transcript.speaker: François Roger
transcript.title: CFO
transcript.content: Thank you, Paul, good morning and good afternoon to all. Let me start with our sales development on slide 11. We have delivered robust results in the second quarter with 8% reported growth and even 10% at constant exchange rates. Our growth is broad-based across businesses and geographies, and hyper-inflationary countries add only a limited contribution to our growth. We are delivering quality growth as you can see on the right-hand side. Our continued portfolio transformation is a key growth driver with strong performance from Dupixent and the ramp-up of our newly launched medicines. Other products also had a significant contribution. Please turn to slide 12. Gross profit showed double-digit growth in line with our sales performance. Gross margin was slightly down due to unfavorable currency impact, Aubagio, and COVID-19 revenue last year. At constant exchange rates, our gross margin has slightly increased, mainly driven by improved product mix. Total operating expenses were up by 5.2% as we invest in marketing and sales to support launches and in R&D. R&D expenses grew double-digit when excluding the one-time EUR 200 million reimbursement from Sobi related to Aubagio. We are fully on track with the step-up of our R&D spend by approximately EUR 700 million this year, totaling around EUR 7.4 billion for 2024. SG&A expenses grew substantially less than sales growth, generating a positive gross leverage impact on margin. Business operating income grew 8.3%, and business EPS growth was up by 4%, driven by higher BOI, partially offset by the higher tax rate of 21%, as well as increased finance costs from higher net debt. Please turn to slide 13. Based on our current performance in the first half of the year, and a strong business outlook for the remainder of the year, we upgrade our earnings per share guidance for 2024 to stable at constant exchange rates. Let me now provide some color on some key considerations for the balance of the year. On Beyfortus, we anticipate the first shipment in the Northern Hemisphere to take place in Q3. Regarding phasing, Q4 sales are likely to be higher than Q3 based on regulatory approvals for the two additional filling lines expected in September. For Flu, we anticipate a phasing with approximately 70% of sales in Q3 and 30% in Q4. Total sales for Flu are expected to decline low single digits versus last year due to unexpectedly softer vaccination rates. Other items are similar to what we shared with you last quarter. Overall, we are pleased with our Q2 commercial and financial performance, with sales growth of 10%, underlying improvement in gross margin, further cost discipline, and continued modernization across the company. This positive momentum in Q2 and the positive outlook for the remainder of the year leads us to upgrade our guidance. With that, I hand over to Houman for further positive news on the pipeline.

transcript.speaker: Houman Ashrafian
transcript.title: Pipeline Lead
transcript.content: Thank you, François. Turning to slide 15. We've achieved several milestones this quarter, showing our continuous pipeline progress. Dupixent for the treatment of COPD was approved last month in the EU, and this is the first time Dupixent has been approved in the EU ahead of the U.S. Further, it is the only biologic medicine approved to treat COPD anywhere. Now, ALTUVIIIO is also approved in the EU under the name Altuvoct. We've received several accepted regulatory submissions, including priority reviews of Dupixent and CRS with MP and adolescents, and Sarclisa in newly diagnosed transplant-ineligible multiple myeloma with U.S. PDUFA dates in H2. Additionally, Fitusiran, our RNA interference antithrombin for patients suffering from hemophilia A and B, has been submitted in the U.S. with a likely regulatory decision early next year. In support of our drive to become a tech-powered biopharma company, we formed a recent collaboration with Formation Bio and OpenAI to accelerate drug development, also supported by the collaboration with Belhara to advance the discovery and drug development of immunology targets, fitting perfectly with our Nurix Research Program STAT6, a key target in immunology. Completing our focus on rare diseases, we've recently announced a development and commercialization agreement outside the U.S. with Fulcrum for losmapimod, AMPK, a map kinase inhibitor, in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, a genetic neuromuscular disease characterized by progressive muscle weakness. This medicine is in phase 3 with an expected data readout by the partner at the end of the year. Moving forward with neurology, we have recently announced an exclusive license agreement with Vigil focusing on a small-molecule phase 1 targeting an area of huge unmet medical need: Alzheimer's disease. These recent activities are helping us to replenish our early-stage projects to ensure the sustainability of our pipeline. Next slide please. At the ATS meeting in May, we presented high-dose phase 2 data from the proof of concept withdrawal design study of rilzabrutinib, our advanced oral treatment targeting both type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation in moderate to severe asthma. At week 12, treatment with high-dose rilzabrutinib resulted in a 36% relative risk reduction in the loss of asthma control events compared to placebo. This extended to a 25% reduction observed in the low-dose cohort. Additionally, we observed a rapid, significantly meaningful improvement in asthma symptoms and quality of life with a well-tolerated safety profile. These positive results demonstrate the potential of rilzabrutinib as an add-on for uncontrolled asthma patients and are part of a broader set of studies to build on the positive phase 3 data in ITP for the regulatory submission expected later this year. On my last slide, I would like to highlight the exciting upcoming news flow for the next 18 months in support of increased R&D productivity. We plan 12 phase 3 readouts, 13 submissions, nine regulatory decisions, and we look forward to keeping you updated on the progress. Before handing back to Paul, I would like to extend my sincere thanks to every colleague in the R&D team for the work they do for patients. We've undergone changes over the past month, and we're well on track with the pipeline of new opportunities as we chase the miracles of science to improve people's lives. With that, I hand back over to Paul for Q&A.

Remember we're seeing many of you again early next week. You'll be notified when your line is open. You can ask your question at that time. Please make sure you unmute your microphone, or alternatively, submit your question by clicking the Q&A icon at the bottom of the screen. Now we'll take the first question. Thomas?

transcript.title: Analyst
transcript.content: Great, thanks for taking my questions. So I think you've talked about two lines adding to one, so can we just assume that's a tripling? And can we read that your phasing comment on Beyfortus so more in the fourth quarter and third quarter to mean that you might not have the manufacturing approved by the beginning of the season in September? And then secondly on Opella, just wondered if you could update us on the timelines in which you expect to be able to clarify to the market the route of separation as the sale versus spin and perhaps just help us understand the factors that go into the decision between the two at this stage. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you. I think there are five questions there. Graham, thanks. I don't know what I need to do, but anyway, Thomas, over to you.

transcript.speaker: Thomas Triomphe
transcript.title: Executive Vice President
transcript.content: Thanks for the question, Graham. So a few elements to address your questions. First of all, we're confident Beyfortus will be a blockbuster in 2024. That's the guidance that we have provided and we fully align with that. You remember the different messages we've shared previously regarding the need to increase supply. We had two filling lines and wanted to ensure that we were doing production at pace with our partner AstraZeneca, while submitting the regulatory applications for the regulatory bodies to approve those lines in due time. We are on track with this plan; we have done production at pace as expected, as well as PPQ batches and validation batches, and submitted the necessary regulatory applications. Now it's in the hands of the regulatory bodies for the exact timing of the approval, which will enable the overall shipment of doses. However, we believe there's every reason to be confident about the accelerated review process of those lines and about the fact that we'll be able to move forward for the supply for the 2024 RSV season. Regarding the indication we've provided on the split in quarters between Q3 and Q4, we have acknowledged the expectation to have Q4 sales above Q3 sales due to the differences in patient demand.

transcript.speaker: François Roger
transcript.title: CFO
transcript.content: Yes, Graham, on Opella, regarding timing, we confirm what we had said before, which means we expect that transaction to take place at the earliest in the fourth quarter of 2024, potentially in the first quarter of 2025. However, it would make a significant difference. I confirm as well that we are still in a very competitive process, with essentially three options. Two of them are public, either an IPO or a spin-off, and one of them could involve a sale to a private party, so the scenario is still open. Our main objective remains value creation for shareholders. To provide some insight into our considerations, two main items we focus on are valuation as of today and the potential future value under different configurations, along with the execution risk—certainty of transaction versus uncertainty is part of what we are analyzing. The good news is the competitive processes, across the various options, generally yield better opportunities to extract value, so we remain positive regarding the quality of our assets.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Okay, thank you. Next question.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Next questions come from the line of Shirley Chang from Barclays. Shirley?

transcript.speaker: Shirley Chang
transcript.title: Analyst
transcript.content: Can you hear me? Thank you, Shirley Chang from Barclays asking questions for Emily Field. We have one question regarding the flu vaccine. Can you please share with us the timeline for the COVID-19 and flu vaccine preparation with Novavax? In addition, how would you comment on the perspective of your vaccine versus a standalone flu vaccine? Also, I noticed that you have an mRNA flu vaccine in phase 1. How would this candidate provide potential synergy or other impacts on your current product launch timeline? Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you. Thomas?

transcript.speaker: Thomas Triomphe
transcript.title: Executive Vice President
transcript.content: Thank you very much, Shirley. A few elements in your question. First point, I understand you were inquiring about the partnership with Novavax and specifically about the combination vaccines. As you mentioned, we want to ensure that there are no compromises in safety or efficacy, and we believe a combination is only worthwhile if it is at least as good as, or better than, the best standalone products. It's perhaps too early to discuss specific timelines, so we haven't shared anything about this. However, it is logical to assume that following this partnership, we aim to move quickly, with clinical operations expected to begin sometime in 2024. Regarding the mRNA flu project, we've moved from one product to another, fully in line with what we discussed at the investors' event last year. We showed that the first generation of mRNA flu was not generating flu titers, flu antibodies, nor had known efficacy, and the safety levels were not at the standards of the current standard of care in flu. Hence, we aim to achieve the next generation of RNA vaccines. Our approach with mRNA flu and combination vaccines is, therefore, the right path to explore. Even with different competitors, where we believe there is a significant compromise on tolerability and possibly efficacy, we consider our focus to be strategically sound. Lastly, we see a synergistic effect rather than a cannibalization effect. As leaders in flu today, we aim to maintain that leadership moving forward.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you, Thomas. Next question.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: The next questions come from the line of Seamus Fernandez, Guggenheim.

transcript.content: Well, thank you so much for the question, Seamus. We are really excited about the COPD launch. As a reminder, we have just received approval in Europe, marking the first-ever advanced therapy to be approved for COPD, which is the third leading cause of death worldwide, making it a really significant moment for us and for patients. Regarding uptake, the good news is we're already interacting with this particular physician population daily for asthma. Additionally, this disease status, as we highlighted, is driven by underlying type 2 inflammation, which is similar to asthma. The opportunity will be to find these patients and ensure they are introduced to therapy promptly. We think most of the growth will primarily materialize by 2025. We plan to launch this year and expect the largest growth will actually come in 2025.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you. Houman, CD40 Ligand?

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you. Next question.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator

transcript.speaker: Jo Walton
transcript.title: Analyst
transcript.content: Thank you. If I can return briefly to Beyfortus, I think we can work out for ourselves the level of demand in the US, and assuming that you have capacity, how you might deal with that. Can you give us a sense of where demand is building outside of the US? Will there be significant new countries you can supply this year, or will other major markets really come in next year? It's really trying to get a sense of the US versus x-US split. As for Fitusiran, which is now a filed asset, could you remind us where you think it'll fit into the hemophilia space, please?

transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Okay, Jo, you’re loud and clear. Thomas, over to you on Beyfortus.

transcript.speaker: Thomas Triomphe
transcript.title: Executive Vice President
transcript.content: Regarding the geographies, thanks for the question, Jo. As you may recall, last year we focused on three significant countries: the U.S., Spain, and France. However, key ones include expected launches in several provinces in Italy, along with anticipated progress in Germany, where we've seen positive recommendations moving forward. Other European countries, like Ireland and Portugal, have also provided relevant recommendations. This gives you a glimpse of how we plan to expand this year.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: And let me just add that Beyfortus is not the reason for the upgrade in guidance today, which is a positive overall. I apologize for anybody offended by Thomas's language. Houman, over to you on Fitusiran.

transcript.speaker: Houman Ashrafian
transcript.title: Pipeline Lead
transcript.content: Hi Jo, thank you for your comment on Fitusiran. Based on the mechanism of action, we believe that Fitusiran is applicable to all patients with hemophilia and will likely be used broadly. The key issue is the major unmet medical need today is in hemophilia B, especially with inhibitors, and I suspect that the immediate use of this medication will be in that group, but it will certainly extend more broadly. It's important to remind everyone that this is a highly differentiated therapy with very clear data. The fact that it is a low-volume treatment with tolerable administration frequency—6 to 12 times a year compared to the manifold treatments required for other categories—makes it significant. Importantly, there is no cold chain needed, and unlike antibodies, this is relatively easy to provide worldwide. This positions it as a highly differentiated therapy, and we maintain optimism about its potential.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Yes, thank you. It has a great profile. However, tailoring and titrating is not uncommon for this patient population, but it has a compelling profile. Next question.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO

This signals the endorsement of Dupixent's profile, and we look forward to the data readout and ultimately bringing this to patients worldwide.

transcript.speaker: Houman Ashrafian
transcript.title: Pipeline Lead
transcript.content: Yes, Luisa, thank you for your question regarding Study C. We are optimistic about efficacy in this patient population; the overall collaboration has accelerated the study by three months and overperformed. We have high hopes for the differentiation of this TL1A, particularly regarding its potency and unique ability to distinguish between the DR3 and decoy 3 receptor, making this version especially unique. We anticipate results, as described, in Q4 of this year. We use this trial to inform both dosing and indication. I should also note that we've enjoyed a productive relationship with our partners, Teva, and following the results, we will guide the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you. Next question.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO

transcript.title: Executive Vice President
transcript.content: Indeed, there is interest in China for Beyfortus. However, it's important to outline that we expect Beyfortus will operate primarily as a private market offering. This approach means a progressive ramp-up. We're beginning from a base in China where disease awareness is quite low, and thus, it will take some time to build it up. Beyfortus is already registered in China; consequently, we are now in the process of engaging with medical professionals, defining forward pathways, increasing awareness, and initiating current for out-of-pocket marketing.

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you. We were in China recently, and we met with senior officials. The interest is building significantly, and we look forward to opening that opportunity when it arises. Next question.

transcript.speaker: Gary Steventon
transcript.title: Analyst
transcript.content: Hi, can you hear me now? Perfect, thank you. First question pertains to vaccines. You're reiterating the mid-single-digit growth target and a bullish Beyfortus target, but you also mentioned a more refined low-single-digit decline for flu, potentially indicating a weaker performance. Essentially, where are the other moving parts in vaccines supporting the mid-single-digit outlook? Is it purely greater confidence in hitting the Beyfortus blockbuster target offsetting flu, or are there other elements in the wider portfolio to consider? Secondly, could you elaborate on how the approved indications for Dupixent are trending towards your unchanged EUR 13 billion target for this year, and whether there are specific strengths or weaknesses regarding particular indications?

transcript.speaker: Paul Hudson
transcript.title: CEO
transcript.content: Thank you, Gary. I think we touched on the relative moving parts for flu and Beyfortus. It's evident there's no magic recipe here; Beyfortus is projected to achieve blockbuster status while flu is exhibiting low single-digit declines. The expected decline is primarily driven by overall market performance. We near the end of the pre-booking season in North America and have mirrored some results with last year, but vaccination rates seem softer this time around, thus affecting our expectations.
